text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday.
- Tourism news: Croatia may be this summer's hit with tour operators in Germany, Austria, Czech Republic and Slovakia according to the latest bookings.
Croatia may see up to 50 percent more tourists from Bosnia this summer, says head of the Tourist Association Marijan Bulat.
Tourists have no reason to fear their safety in Croatia, says Deputy Interior Minister Zlatko Gledec.
- Serb Orthodox patrirarch Pavle, visiting last Serb enclave of Eastern Slavonia, asked Serbs to stay in the area and respect the Croatian authorities.

- Jumbo posters promoting parties for pending local elections lack any imagination, featuring party leaders sporting artificial smiles. Only the ruling HDZ party's campaign is said to have shown some visual inventiveness.
- Editorial: Croatia is not an overindebted country, its foreign debt totalling $4.9 billion in December 1996. But the country must be cautious in the long-run and encourage domestic savings.
- Statistics: January agricultural foreign trade deficit put at $17.6 million. Farming still under pressure from cheaper imports.
- Reporters Sans Frontieres have not yet put Sinisa Glavasevic, famous radio reporter from Vukovar, on their list of journalists who were killed or went missing in the war in former Yugoslavia.

- Croatia is planning to integrate its river traffic with the rest of Europe. A channel between the Danube and the Sava rivers between Vukovar and Slavonski Samac on the Bosnian border is being mulled to shorten traffic.
- Banking news: German Commerzbank AG officials on a fact-gathering mission to Croatia. The bank is believed to be contemplating opening of a branch in Zagreb soon.
- County court in the port of Rijeka opened a new trial of five Moslems accused of planning to assassinate former rebel Moslem tycoon Fikret Abdic.

- Most serious candidates for the recently vacated post of Economy Minister are head of the electricity board (HEP), Damir Begovic, and economic advisor at the Croatian embassy in the Washington, Nenad Porges.

- Croat police in the divided Bosnian town of Mostar has issued a list of 21 people arrested in the city and its surroundings, following the police crackdown on criminals after a February incident when one Moslem was killed and some 20 wounded.

- Constitutional court brushed off a complaint by the Mostar warlord Mladen Naletilic Tuta against a Zagreb municipal court's decision to keep him in prison, pending results of the ongoing investigation against him for kidnapping and murder. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
